prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Create ONE landscape repair atlas containing exactly SIX complete circular painted tokens in THREE columns and TWO rows. REFERENCE 1 is icons-05, REFERENCE 2 is icons-06, REFERENCE 3 is icons-08, and REFERENCE 4 is icons-01. Every reference is a five-column four-row source atlas. The first three supply the specific token edit targets; the fourth supplies the stable rocky-world landform. Select only the specified subjects, preserve their established composition and visual character except for the explicit corrections, and do not copy any complete reference sheet.

Preserve the existing luminous opaque gouache, selective fine ink, strong simplified silhouettes at 64px, textured deep lapis grounds, jade/turquoise water and foliage, burnt ochre land, muted coral, warm ivory light and very narrow ivory-gold rims. Each token is a perfect circle centered within its equal square grid cell, diameter 80 percent of the shorter cell side; painted interiors are opaque, exterior and generous gutters transparent. All six tokens have matching rim weight and visual scale. No text, labels, numbers, grid lines, watermark, modern equipment, houses or cast shadows outside circles.

Mandatory causal and identity corrections: planetary tilt belongs to the same rocky PLANET, never the Sun; the Seasons Sun has NO axis line. Recovering world and World after the ice have NO giant footprint marks of any kind, no dark footprint pits and no returned browsing giants. Evidence of past loss is OLD NATURALLY FALLEN WOOD among changed woodland. Renewing forest and Forest rain belong to the early FERN-TREE forest family with tall trunks and splayed divided fronds, not later broadleaf/flowering woodland; broken wood has torn splintered ends, never a flat human-cut stump.

Exact order, left to right then top to bottom:

CELL 1, TOP LEFT, Axial tilt. Source: REFERENCE 2 row 2 column 4. Replace the cloudy gas-giant body with the SAME ROCKY WORLD geography in REFERENCE 4 row 4 column 3: the large unmistakable ochre hook-shaped landform and two short satellite ridges. This later world has jade sea between its solid landforms. Retain the tilted polar axis, crossing the PLANET centre from one pole to the other, and one small rotation arc around the upper pole. No swirling atmospheric bands, gas-giant appearance, axis through a sun or replacement with Earth continents. Target subject: The same rocky planet retains its recognizable hook-shaped ochre continent and two smaller satellite ridges, now surrounded by jade sea; a single thin ivory polar axis passes through the planet on a clear diagonal against a faint horizontal orbital plane. A small rotation arc circles one planetary pole, while the land and sea remain exposed rather than replaced by gas-giant cloud swirls.

CELL 2, TOP CENTRE, Seasons. Source: REFERENCE 2 row 2 column 5. Preserve the four seasonal branch arrangement and central golden Sun, but REMOVE the long diagonal line passing through the SUN entirely. Use the SAME branch fork and twig silhouette in four states: new spring leaves, full summer foliage, ochre falling autumn leaves, and bare snow-touched winter twigs. No solar axis, solar poles, rotation line or tilt diagram attached to the Sun; do not move that line onto an unrelated object. Target subject: Four recognizably seasonal views of the same forked branch form a loose ring around a golden Sun: fresh spring leaves, dense summer foliage, ochre autumn leaves falling and a bare snow-touched winter twig. The Sun is an ordinary clear disk with no axis, pole line or rotation arc through or around it.

CELL 3, TOP RIGHT, Recovering world. Source: REFERENCE 3 row 1 column 5. Remove EVERY large fresh footprint, dark track depression and crater-like mark from the curved hillside, replacing the entire trail with naturally continuous soil and mixed young woodland. No fossil footprint slab either. Keep the small mammal and pollinator, and preserve the living-world composition. At the edge of the new woodland show a little OLD CHARRED FALLEN WOOD with natural splintered ends as the surviving trace of loss, not living giants. Preserve the familiar ochre hooked landform and jade coastal water where visible. Target subject: The familiar curved ochre world and hooked coastline support a mixed young forest with a small furred mammal and an insect pollinator at its living edge. Old naturally splintered, charred fallen wood remains among the different new growth as evidence of loss; no giant footprints, track depressions, fossil-track slab or living great browsers appear anywhere.

CELL 4, BOTTOM LEFT, World after the ice. Source: REFERENCE 3 row 3 column 3. Remove EVERY large footprint, track depression and crater-like mark from the hillside; the ground is naturally continuous restored woodland and a reopened jade river. The ice has RETREATED to the far high horizon rather than advancing into the foreground. Preserve small mammals, the familiar hook-shaped ochre world geography and jade water, and a little old fallen wood within the changed woodland. Absolutely no fresh giant tracks, no fossil track display and no living giant browsers. Target subject: The same curved world retains its hook-shaped ochre land and jade water, with ice withdrawn to the far high horizon, a free-flowing river and restored woodland spreading over open lower ground among small mammals. A little old fallen wood remains within the changed forest, but no giant footprints, track depressions or living great browsers appear.

CELL 5, BOTTOM CENTRE, Renewing forest. Source: REFERENCE 1 row 2 column 2, with frond anatomy from REFERENCE 1 row 1 column 2. Replace the broadleaf sapling and flat-topped cut stump with NEW SMALL FERN TREES growing among the SAME EARLY FERN FOREST family: upright trunks with splayed crowns of long clearly divided fern fronds. Roots draw on dark soil beside decaying old wood. The old trunks are naturally SNAPPED AND SPLINTERED, with jagged torn fibers and irregular broken tops, never flat horizontal saw-cut surfaces. No axe, saw, cut marks, modern logging, broadleaf saplings, flowers or fruit. Preserve the soil/roots/deadwood renewal relationship and restrained tall forest background. Target subject: Small new fern trees with splayed divided fronds grow among taller trunks of the same early fern forest, their roots reaching into rich soil beside old naturally snapped and splintered trunks and decaying wood. Every broken trunk has an irregular torn end, with no flat saw-cut stump, axe marks, tools or broadleaf sapling replacing the fern family.

CELL 6, BOTTOM RIGHT, Forest rain. Source: REFERENCE 1 row 2 column 5, with frond anatomy from REFERENCE 1 row 1 column 2. Replace the modern rounded broadleaf crowns with the SAME TALL FERN FOREST: straight visible trunks topped by splayed radial crowns of long divided fronds, not solid leafy balls. Preserve the pale moisture wisps rising FROM THE FROND CANOPY to the low cloud and the returning rain curtain at the far side. Keep rising moisture and falling rain spatially distinct and readable. No flowering trees, broadleaf canopy, fruit or modern plantation rows. Target subject: The same tall early fern forest raises straight trunks into a canopy of splayed, clearly divided jade fronds; fine pale moisture wisps rise from that canopy into a low cloud that rains over the far edge of the forest. Keep the frond crowns distinct rather than replacing them with rounded flowering or broadleaf tree canopies.

Before completing the atlas, keep all six corrected subjects distinct: tilted rocky planet; four seasonal versions of one branch around an unmarked Sun; recovering mixed young woodland with old fallen wood and no tracks; post-ice river and woods with distant retreated ice and no tracks; young fern trees among splintered dead trunks; tall fern canopy returning moisture to a rain cloud. Do not add extra icons or new symbolic diagrams.
